identity.title: An independent hybrid imaging of Sgr A* from the data in EHT 2017 observations
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we report the results of our analysis of the public EHT data of the Sgr A$^{*}$.

evidence.loc: 1.2 Prior radio research of Sgr A*
evidence.quote: The distance from the Earth to the Galactic center is about 8 kpc

question.value: Is the ring structure reported by the EHTC for Sgr A* real, or an artifact of the bumpy EHT 2017 PSF? Independent hybrid-mapping reimaging of the public EHT 2017 data.

evidence.quote: We propose that the ring structure found by the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration (EHTC) as the black hole shadow of Sgr A$^{*}$ is an artifact by the bumpy PSF (Point Spread Function) of the EHT2017.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: two recording channels at 227.1 and 229.1 GHz

arrays.value: EHT 2017, eight stations including ALMA and SPT

evidence.quote: The EHT observed Sgr A$^{*}$ in early April 2017 with a total of eight stations, including the Antarctic station

angular_resolution.value: default restoring beam 23.0x15.3 uas, PA 66.6 deg; ~20 uas

evidence.quote: yields a default restoring beam of $\mathrm{(FWHM) =23.0\times15.3~\mu \rm as}$ and $\mathrm{PA= 66.6^{\circ}}$

observing_dates.value: EHT 2017; analysis of April 7 data (April 6 in appendix)

evidence.quote: Our data analysis focused on the April 7 data, which the EHTC analyzed in detail

provided.value: Network-calibrated, HOPS-calibrated, LMT-corrected, normalized April 7 visibilities

evidence.quote: Namely we analyzed data from April 7, i.e., calibrated by HOP, corrected for amplitude with respect to LMT, and normalized for time variability using measured intensities.

what.value: EHTC ring image digitized from Figure 3 for residual comparison; ring diameter 51.8±2.3 uas, shadow 48.7±7.0 uas

evidence.quote: we digitized Figure 3 in (cite: EHTC2022a) to obtain each coordinate value and the intensity at that coordinate.

what.value: Intrinsic size and scattering scaling used for expected shape

evidence.quote: Assuming that the intrinsic angular size of Sgr A$^{*}$ is proportional to the observed wavelength (cite: Johnson:2018)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Simulated UVMOD datasets (noise only; 1 Jy point source) with EHT 2017 uv coverage, self-calibrated on ring models

evidence.quote: We created two simulated data sets by using a AIPS task, UVMOD.

archive_products_used_as_is.value: Public EHTC HOPS-calibrated data used as released

evidence.quote: We selected the HOP-calibrated datasets because the CASA calibration data show a large difference in closure amplitude between channels of the raw data

self_calibration.value: phase-only self-cal, six steps, SOLINT=0.15 min, point-source initial model; no amplitude self-cal

evidence.quote: The six steps of self-calibration were performed in phase-only mode.
Data calibration using self-calibration solutions for amplitude was omitted due to the significant intensity variations in Sgr A$^{*}$

task.value: AIPS IMAGR CLEAN with hybrid mapping

evidence.quote: hybrid mapping technique, which is commonly used in VLBI imaging and implemented in AIPS

masking.value: FOV 1 mas square; CLEAN BOX 256 uas diameter

evidence.quote: the CLEAN subtraction area is restricted by the BOX setting ($\mathrm{256~\mu \rm as}$ in diameter)

final_beam.value: Gaussian beam 25 uas used for alternate image convolution

evidence.quote: a $\mathrm{25~\mu \rm as}$ Gaussian beam is used to convolve the CLEAN components

what.value: SOLINT in CALIB set shorter than coherence time following earlier approach

evidence.quote: following the same approach as in CALIB in (cite: Miyoshi2022a)

what.value: LMT amplitude gains pre-corrected assuming 60 uas source size

evidence.quote: According to Section 2-2 of (cite: EHTC2022c), the LMT amplitude gains were pre-corrected assuming a $\mathrm{60~\mu \rm as}$ source size

unstated_but_needed: IMAGR ROBUSTNESS, GAIN and NITER values for the final image
Which candidate maps were averaged and how the final image was chosen

method.value: Iterate CLEAN imaging and phase-only self-calibration from a point-source start; choose among candidate images by residuals

evidence.quote: We started the hybrid mapping with a point source as the initial image model

key_parameters.value: SOLINT = 0.15 min, SNR cutoff 3, REFANT ALMA

evidence.quote: APARM(7) (SNR cut off)

validation.value: Compared residuals of normalized amplitude, closure phase and closure amplitude, and PSF features

evidence.quote: compared the residuals of closure phases, closure amplitudes, and normalized amplitudes

analysis_steps.goal: Compare with EHTC ring via visibility residuals

method.value: Digitized EHTC image converted to visibilities with UVMOD at 1 Jy and residuals computed vs data

evidence.quote: this numerical image data was input into the AIPS task, UVMOD, to create a visibility set

evidence.loc: 4.2.1 Residuals of normalized amplitude of our final image compared to those of the EHTC ring
evidence.quote: Our final image consistently exhibits smaller means and standard deviations in the residuals than the case of the EHTC ring image, regardless of the integration time between $\mathrm{T_{\text{int}} = 10~sec}$ and $\mathrm{T_{\text{int}} = 900~sec}$.

method.value: Self-calibrate noise-only and point-source data with ring models then CLEAN with narrow BOX; rings 30-70 uas

evidence.quote: We made rings with diameters ranging from $\mathrm{30}$ to $\mathrm{70~\mu \rm as}$

evidence.loc: 5.2 Rings from the simulated data of other structures
evidence.quote: It can be seen that the ring image with a diameter of $\mathrm{50~\mu \rm as}$ shows the largest value and is the most plausible image among them.

method.value: Brightness ratio of east peak to west dark spot gives v/c cosθ; radius and inclination derived

evidence.quote: $\frac{v}{c}\cos\theta =  0.438.$

assumptions.value: D=8 kpc, M=4e6 Msun, optically thin edge-on disk

evidence.quote: Assuming a distance to the Galactic Center of $\mathrm{D_{GC} = 8 kpc}$ and a black hole mass of $\mathrm{4\times10^6M_{\odot}}$

used_for.value: Hybrid mapping, CALIB, IMAGR, UVMOD, DBCON

evidence.quote: implemented in AIPS (the NRAO Astronomical Image Processing System

evidence.quote: $\mathrm{NR_{ours} = 0.080 \pm 0.397}$

results_numeric.quantity: Normalized amplitude residual, EHTC ring (Tint=180 s)

evidence.quote: $\mathrm{NR_{EHTC} = 0.862 \pm 1.552}$
$\mathrm{Res_{cp} = 0.2 \pm 58.1^\circ}$
which is $\mathrm{49.09~\mu \rm as}$
the viewing angle is estimated to be $\mathrm{\theta \sim 43.8 ^{\circ}}$

findings_qualitative.value: Final image is east-west elongated with brighter east side, not a ring

evidence.quote: our final image of Sgr A$^{*}$shows an east-west elongation with an asymmetry, the east side appearing brighter than the west side.

findings_qualitative.value: Closure quantities differ between the two recording channels in all public data, suggesting internal inconsistency

evidence.quote: an unexplained closure discrepancy between recording channels is present in all EHTC data

claims.hypothesis: EHTC ring is a PSF artifact
claims.experiment: Rings reproduced from noise-only and point-source simulated data with ring-model self-cal and narrow BOX
claims.result: Ring images produced, best at 50 uas
claims.finding: Ring can arise from the PSF and self-cal

evidence.loc: 5.2 Rings from the simulated data of other structures
evidence.quote: This result is one of important indications that the EHT 2017 *u-v* coverage is insufficient to accurately reproduce the observed object’s structure and is likely to yield results consistent with the assumed image.

claims.hypothesis: Hybrid mapping gives a more consistent image than the EHTC ring
claims.experiment: Residual comparison of normalized amplitudes and closures
claims.result: Half the amplitude residuals, comparable closure residuals

evidence.quote: We believe that our image is more reliable than the EHTC image because our image shows half the residuals of the EHTC image in normalized visibility amplitude

limitations_admitted.value: Fine structure not very reliable; the west dark spot disappears with 25 uas beam

evidence.quote: the reliability of the fine structure seen in Figure 2 (a) is not very high.

referee_caveats_inferred: Image selected by authors' own residual metric; both images have large residuals
Simulations use deliberately extreme self-cal and BOX
Doppler interpretation rests on single pixels

data_public_as_stated.value: EHTC public data; derived products on request

evidence.quote: The original observational data are available on the EHTC website.

reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and AIPS but key imaging parameters are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Recipe incomplete and the result depends on subjective image selection.

fixed.new: Our final image consistently exhibits smaller means and standard deviations in the residuals than the case of the EHTC ring image, regardless of the integration time between $\mathrm{T_{\text{int}} = 10~sec}$ and $\mathrm{T_{\text{int}} = 900~sec}$.
It can be seen that the ring image with a diameter of $\mathrm{50~\mu \rm as}$ shows the largest value and is the most plausible image among them.

This result is one of important indications that the EHT 2017 *u-v* coverage is insufficient to accurately reproduce the observed object’s structure and is likely to yield results consistent with the assumed image.
We believe that our image is more reliable than the EHTC image because our image shows half the residuals of the EHTC image in normalized visibility amplitude
